The polar curve $r=6$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{2\pi }{3}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. What are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$
worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $P$ are $(r,\theta )=(6,\frac{2\pi }{3}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $P$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =6\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-3 \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\pi }{3}) \\  & =6\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =3\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(-3,3\sqrt{3}).$
